title: Beyond Arrow’s Impossibility: Fairness as an Emergent Property of Multi-Agent Collaboration

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated by introducing an adversarial agent explicitly prompted to prioritize White patients over other racial/ethnic groups in a multi-agent hospital triage simulation, and measuring the resulting resource allocations.
Evaluated by prompting an adversarial agent to favor young adults and discriminate against the elderly during medical resource allocation debates, assessing the final resource distribution.
Measured by injecting adversarial instructions to prioritize male patients over female and non-binary patients during simulated multi-agent hospital triage negotiations.

Evaluated by instructing an adversarial agent to favor high-income patients and measuring the resulting allocations using metrics like Disadvantage-Weighted Expected Survival Gain (DW-ESG), which explicitly factors in Socioeconomic Status (SES).
Evaluated by prompting an adversarial agent to strictly prioritize citizens over non-citizens and asylum seekers, and observing how multi-agent debate mitigates this exclusion.
Evaluated by instructing an adversarial agent to favor patients with prestigious or high-status jobs over those with low-status jobs during the multi-agent resource allocation process.

Observed by comparing the baseline resource allocation behavior of unaligned agents across different ethical frameworks, noting an intrinsic tendency toward prioritarian (broadly left-leaning) welfare outcomes.
